items.title: Algerian police seize 33 kg of cocaine in major drug bust
items.description: Algerian police released video on Thursday reportedly showing the results of a major drug bust. Police said they seized some 33 kilos of cocaine and more than 10 million capsules of the psychotropic substance pregabalin.

items.title: Drone strike wounds 13 in Tigray capital as fears of renewed war grow
items.description: A drone strike on Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region, injured at least 13 people, including five children, a hospital official said Thursday. The attack comes amid growing tensions between federal and Tigrayan forces and fears the region could slide back into war.

items.title: Nissan management shake-up plans reported as sharks circle

items.title: Spain battles forest fire a short drive from flash flood
items.description: The blaze, near Valencia, forced more than 1,000 people from their homes. In nearby Catalonia, civil defense teams carried out 200 rescue operations after floods trapped residents in cars and homes.

items.title: Benin cyberactivist Steve Amoussou freed after two-year sentence
items.description: Beninese cyberactivist Steve Amoussou has been released after serving a two-year prison sentence for charges including politically motivated insult and spreading false news. His case had become a prominent test of the government's treatment of critics and online dissent.

items.title: DRC, M23 agree peace roadmap as Doha talks seek to regain momentum
items.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo and the Rwanda-backed M23 have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks, setting out the next steps and timetable under the Doha framework. The deal comes after months of stalled diplomacy and renewed fighting in the east.

items.title: Ukraine news: UK PM Burnham arrives in Kyiv to show support
items.description: Andy Burnham's first trip abroad as PM will see him co-chair a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing and meet with Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The visit comes as Ukraine marks its 35th independence day. DW has more.

items.title: UEFA chief Ceferin calls for Infantino to quit but rules out replacing him
items.description: Aleksander Ceferin, president of the European soccer confederation (UEFA) has announced that he will not run against Gianni Infantino but warned the under-fire FIFA president that he must either quit or face a leadership challenge in March. Infantino has been mired in a crisis since the failure of his controversial – and ultimately abandoned – plan to open FIFA to private investors.

items.title: Munich prosecutors close fatal 1970 antisemitic arson case
items.description: Prosecutors and police in Munich believe they have identified the man who set a 1970 fire at a Jewish community center and old people's home that killed seven people. But he died in 2020, so prosecution is not possible.

items.title: Toyota eyes lunar rover powered by regenerative fuel-cell tech
items.description: Toyota has teamed up with JAXA since 2019 to develop the manned lunar rover — which it dubbed the Lunar Cruiser — that they hope can be put on the moon in 2029.

items.title: Zelenskyy repeats Ukraine not behind Nord Stream attack
items.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was assisting German authorities with their investigation into the Nord Stream explosions. A second Ukrainian national was arrested in connection with the blasts.

items.title: Fidelity Bank gets extension to publish H1 2026 audited results
items.description: Fidelity Bank said the extension became necessary because the audit of its H1 2026 financial statements is still being finalised. The post Fidelity Bank gets extension to publish H1 2026 audited results appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .

items.title: Fast-moving wildfire amid shifting winds threatens Reno, Nevada, forcing thousands to evacuate
items.description: The Hawk Fire began on Saturday (August 24) and quickly grew to more than 60 sq km as it spread across the Peavine Peak area of the Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest, where rugged foothills are ringed by homes and businesses near the California state line.

items.title: French presidential hopeful Philippe vows to crack down on immigration to Mayotte
items.description: During a visit to Mayotte on Friday, France’s former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe vowed to crack down on immigration to the French overseas territory if he’s elected to the presidency next year.

items.title: Europe ramps up support to Ukraine as its US-dependent air defence runs low
items.description: European leaders are meeting Kyiv as Ukraine holds celebrations for its 35th Independence Day. The so-called Coalition of the Willing is set to hold talks regarding support to the country, four-and-a-half years after the Russian invasion started, with the European Union having announced it was releasing over six billion euros in aid. But US support to Kyiv regarding critical air defence is still missing. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
